views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Implement the already-committed proportional retaliation against the US Section 301 tariffs (scheduled to hit July 6), targeting politically sensitive US exports such as soybeans, autos and aircraft, while simultaneously keeping negotiation channels open and avoiding any disproportionate escalation that would hand Washington a pretext to activate the threatened $200B/$450B tranche. We should match the July 6 List 1 action firmly and signal readiness to talk, but not trigger the maximal escalation on our own initiative.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat to Chinese interests is high and rising. USTR finalized a $50B two-stage tech-focused tariff plan on June 15 (List 1 effective July 6), and on June 18 Trump directed preparation of another $200B at 10%, doubling if we retaliate — threatening up to ~$450B, roughly 90% of our exports to the US. This is aimed directly at Made-in-China-2025 tech sectors, and the April ZTE denial order shows the US is willing to use firm-level, non-tariff targeting. The FX channel is already biting: the renminbi had its worst single month against the dollar in 25 years in June (−3.25%, crossing 6.7) and Shanghai equities fell ~7.5%, though reserves rose a fifth straight month and capital controls + a PBOC RRR cut give us cushion. On the action side, our stated position ('does not want a trade war but must respond strongly') reflects real domestic-political constraints — backing down now would be read as capitulation and invite further demands. But the correct response to this high threat is proportional retaliation, not maximal escalation: China imports only ~$130–150B from the US and cannot match dollar-for-dollar at the $200B/$450B scale, so escalating beyond a fair, symmetrical match would risk an unwinnable spiral that hurts our own export economy and provides the excuse for Trump to double down. Retaliating on politically sensitive US farm/auto/aircraft imports meanwhile maximizes leverage against Trump's base and reinforces our position as defender of the multilateral trade order, while leaving room to negotiate before the larger tranche is ever implemented.
key_factors: Section 301 $50B plan finalized June 15, List 1 effective July 6 (next day)
Trump June 18 threat of additional $200B at 10%, doubling if China retaliates (~$450B / ~90% of Chinese exports)
ZTE denial order April 16 — firm-level non-tariff targeting precedent
Renminbi worst single month vs USD in 25 years (June, -3.25%, past 6.7), Shanghai equities -7.5%
Reserves rose 5th straight month (June) + PBOC RRR cut = financial cushion, capital controls firm
China 'does not want a trade war but must respond strongly' — limited domestic room to back down
China imports only ~$130-150B from US; cannot match dollar-for-dollar at $200B/$450B scale

sources_cited.excerpt: USTR announces final two-stage $50B tariff plan: 25% on List 1 (~$34B effective July 6) and List 2 (~$16B). China announces matching retaliation same day.
Trump directs USTR to identify additional ~$200B of Chinese imports for 10% tariffs if China retaliates against $50B action.
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). Major non-tariff escalation.
Yuan crossed 6.7/dollar first time since Aug 2017; 3.25% fall in June, worst in 25 years; reserves rose for fifth straight month in June.
Trump threatens $200B more and doubling; China MOFCOM warned of comprehensive strong countermeasures; Beijing cannot match dollar-for-dollar.
Beijing: tariffs on $200B more is 'extreme pressure and blackmail'; 'China does not want to fight a trade war... but has to give a strong comeback.'
